title: mriqc 26.0.0 released
post: - Docker: docker pull nipreps/mriqc:26.0.0 (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64) - PyPI: pip install mriqc==26.0.0 (Python 3.13 or newer) The first release of the 26.x series, and the first since 24.0.2 (25.0.0rc0 was never finalized). MRIQC now requires Python 3.13 or newer, following SPEC 0 (https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0000/), and its container image runs on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 .

title: mriqc 26.1.0 released
post: - Docker: docker pull nipreps/mriqc:26.1.0 (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64) - PyPI: pip install mriqc==26.1.0 (Python 3.13 or newer) The first minor release of the 26.x series. MRIQC now supports FLAIR images, and a fix to the head mask changes the background IQMs of every anatomical run.

title: Assessing the Psychedelic “After-Glow” in Ayahuasca Users: Post-Acute Neurometabolic and Functional Connectivity Changes Are Associated with Enhanced Mindfulness Capacities
post: Ayahuasca is a plant tea containing the psychedelic 5-HT2A agonist N,N-dimethyltryptamine and harmala monoamine-oxidase inhibitors. Acute administration leads to neurophysiological modifications in brain regions of the default mode network, purportedly through a glutamatergic mechanism. Post-acutely, ayahuasca potentiates mindfulness capacities in volunteers and induces rapid and sustained antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant patients.

title: Subacute effects of the psychedelic ayahuasca on the salience and default mode networks
post: Neuroimaging studies have just begun to explore the acute effects of psychedelics on large-scale brain networks' functional organization. Even less is known about the neural correlates of subacute effects taking place days after the psychedelic experience.

title: Single-dose Effects of Ayahuasca Compared to Esketamine on Experimentally Induced Pain
post: This was a randomized, parallel, double-blind clinical trial with healthy volunteers Conditions: Healthy Adult Participants. Interventions: Ayahuasca, Esketamine 0.2 mg/kg. Sponsor: University of Sao Paulo. Planned enrolment: 20. Countries: Brazil. Primary outcomes: Subjective pain; Pain tolerance.

title: Psilocybin for Amblyopia - Targeting Critical Periods in Humans
post: The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether ingestion of a drug called psilocybin can increase the effectiveness of amblyopia therapy in adults with amblyopia. Psilocybin is a naturally-occurring psychoactive compound found in many species of mushrooms.

title: Psilocybin FCR Early-Stage Breast Cancer
post: This trial is designed to evaluate efficacy and psychological mechanisms of single-dose psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy (PAP) to treat fear of cancer recurrence (FCR), psychiatric (anxiety, depression) distress and quality-of-life (QOL), in 100 outpatients with early-stage breast cancer.

title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
post: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed.

title: The C. elegans Connectome Toolbox: an open, extensible framework for multimodal connectomic data integration and analysis
post: The nematode C. elegans is one of the best studied model organisms in biology. Since the initial description of the C. elegans neuronal connectome by White and colleagues, numerous studies have mapped and analyzed the connectome, and released structured datasets of the connectivity, often merging and adding to previous versions.

title: Somnus, a tunable, open-source platform for automated EEG sleep scoring in physiological and disease mouse models.
venue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
venue_clean: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
post: Many studies using mouse models of human brain disorders rely on extended recordings of brain electrical activity through electroencephalogram, or EEG.

title: Personalized Prediction of Differences in fMRI Connectivity Estimates Across Preprocessing Pipelines
post: Longitudinal functional MRI of the human brain is valuable for tracking changes in functional connectivity (FC) associated with disease progression or treatment response. Even so, measured FC values depend on preprocessing, and nuisance regression and temporal filtering affect individuals differently.

title: Chronic Mild Stress in Male Wistar-Kyoto Rats Induces Long-Term Hippocampal Plasticity Impairments Differentially Reversed by Acute and Chronic Ketamine Treatment.
post: Chronic stress induces strong alteration of hippocampal synaptic plasticity, impairing long-term potentiation and facilitating long-term depression, processes thought to be involved in the pathophysiology of depression. Ketamine, a noncompetitive antagonist of the N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor, has emerged as a fast-acting antidepressant whose action is believed to involve restoring impaired plasticity, though its sustained effects are elusive.

title: 10 Hz repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for nitrous oxide dependence: a case report
post: Nitrous oxide (N 2 O) abuse has emerged as an increasingly serious public health concern, yet effective interventions for N 2 O dependence remain lacking.

title: From Evidence to Practice: A Systematic Review of Implementation of Psychedelic-Assisted Psychotherapy.
post: Evidence supporting psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy (PAP) for treating posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, and other historically difficult to treat mental health disorders is growing rapidly. Interest from the public and within the US government to provide access to these treatments has also grown.

title: A multi-institutional investigation of psilocybin's effects on mouse behavior.
post: Studies reporting novel therapeutic effects of psychedelic drugs are rapidly emerging. However, the reproducibility and reliability of these findings could remain uncertain for years. Here, we implemented a multi-institutional collaborative approach to define the robust and replicable effects of the psychedelic drug psilocybin on mouse behavior.

title: Intermittent theta burst stimulation to extend early ketamine response in treatment-resistant depression: A preliminary enriched randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.
post: Ketamine produces rapid antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant depression (TRD), but these benefits diminish within days. Whether intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) can sustain ketamine response and whether such effects are associated with changes in large-scale brain networks are unclear.

title: Psychedelics in neurosurgery: Potential utility in prevention, perioperative care, pain management, and neurorehabilitation.
post: Neurosurgical patients carry a high and frequently undertreated burden of psychological suffering, acute and chronic pain, and neurological deficits amenable to recovery. The resurgence of psychedelic research has produced relevant evidence in adjacent fields, but its applicability to neurosurgery has not been systematized.

title: Anesthesia via Dissociative Overload: A Unified Theoretical Framework Linking DMT and Ketamine Through Sigma-1 Convergence, Entropic Saturation, and Workspace Flooding
post: General anesthesia has long been understood as a unitary phenomenon driven by neural suppression — a reduction in cortical activity, entropy, and complexity that renders the brain unable to sustain conscious processing.

title: Slow power-envelope associations among brain, heart, and gut signals during sleep: an exploratory multivariate transfer entropy study.
post: Sleep and the brain-gut axis both involve the coordinated regulation of the central nervous system (CNS), autonomic nervous system (ANS), and enteric nervous system.

title: Temporal imprecision of the self in drug-free psychosis: Abnormal infraslow phase dynamics and brain complexity
post: Self-disturbance is a core feature of schizophrenia (SCZ) and may emerge during the prodromal phase. Temporal imprecision has recently been proposed as a core neural mechanism in schizophrenia, primarily demonstrated in faster EEG frequency ranges.

title: Brain-heart decoupling in somatic depression: Desynchronization between salience network neuropsychological connectivity and heart rate variability.
post: Somatic depression is a distinct subtype of major depressive disorder, with a poorer response to treatment, an elevated risk of suicidal behaviour, and a worse prognosis. Interoception, the sense of internal bodily signals, is related to somatic symptoms.

title: Directional brain-heart interaction during cognitive workload: a permutation conditional mutual information approach
post: The functional interaction between the central nervous system and autonomic cardiovascular regulation, commonly referred to as Brain-Heart Interaction (BHI), has gained increasing attention in neurology and psychology through the joint analysis of Electroencephalography (EEG) and Electrocardiography (ECG) signals.

title: Comprehensive benchmarking of EEG biomarkers for Parkinson's disease: robustness, reliability, and clinical discriminability across multiple datasets.
post: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a high-temporal-resolution, noninvasive window into some of the abnormalities underlying Parkinson's disease (PD), yet reported electrophysiological biomarkers vary widely across studies due to differences in preprocessing, feature extraction, and analytical pipelines.

title: The application of transcranial magnetic stimulation in treatment-resistant depression: insights from omics.
post: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) is a refractory form of major depressive disorder (MDD) for which conventional antidepressant strategies are often insufficient. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) has demonstrated clinical efficacy in TRD, but its biological mechanisms remain incompletely understood.

title: Vasomechanic treatment is associated with increased efflux of human brain proteins.
post: An age-related neurovascular impairment in nitric oxide (NO)-mediated vasodilation and reciprocal Piezo1-dependent vascular vasoconstriction may precede the accumulation of soluble brain proteins such as amyloid-β (Aβ) and disruption of brain fluid homeostasis in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Preclinical studies suggest that restoring these pathways can enhance neurofluid transport and improve cognitive outcomes.

title: Disrupting the semantic network shifts activity to domain-general brain regions.
post: Semantic processing relies on flexible interactions between specialized lexico-semantic regions and domain-general control networks, particularly under challenging conditions. Using transcranial magnetic stimulation interleaved with functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigated acute network adaptation when the left posterior middle temporal gyrus-a core lexico-semantic region-was perturbed during lexico-semantic decisions in 25 healthy participants.

title: Disruptions in brain hierarchical organisation reveal Alzheimer's disease progression
post: Alzheimer’s disease arises from interacting amyloid, tau, and neurodegenerative processes, and is associated with large-scale network dysfunction and reduced brain dynamics complexity. However, it remains unclear whether disease progression alters the causal hierarchical organisation of large-scale brain dynamics.

title: Multi-receptor whole-brain modeling reveals affinity-driven chemoarchitectural mechanism of virtual atomoxetine action
post: Linking molecular mechanisms with large-scale brain dynamics remains a fundamental challenge in computational psychiatry. Receptor-informed whole-brain models have provided mechanistic insights into pharmacological interventions, yet they have largely relied on single-receptor topographies that cannot explain the collective response of multiple receptor systems.

title: A General-Purpose Adaptable Foundation Model for Total-Body PET Kinetic Modelling.
post: Voxel-level kinetic modeling in total-body dynamic positron emission tomography (TB-PET) enables precise physiological quantification but complicates parameter uncertainty estimation. While generative consistency models (CMs) can rapidly estimate Bayesian posterior distributions, they are constrained by type of tracers, kinetic models, and protocols.

title: A Comparison and Validation of BIDS Apps for Preprocessing of [ 11 C]UCB-J PET data
post: Preprocessing of Positron Emission Tomography (PET) data can be performed in many different ways and often involves manual steps, resulting in reduced comparability across analyses and pipelines.

title: Working memory neural correlates after ketamine in treatment-resistant depression: a randomized placebo-controlled functional magnetic resonance imaging study.
post: Ketamine exerts rapid antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant depression (TRD), but its impact on working memory and neural circuitry remains unclear. This secondary analysis investigated behavioral and neural changes during a working memory task post-ketamine infusion in TRD participants versus healthy volunteers (HVs).

title: Pathway-selective Gi1, but not Gq, protein activation distinguishes hallucinogenic from non-hallucinogenic serotonin 5-HT2A receptor agonists in the human cortex.
post: The serotonin 5-HT 2A receptor (5-HT 2A R) signaling involves canonical G q/11 proteins and alternative pathways, such as recruitment of other G proteins. It has been proposed that the 5-HT 2A R-mediated activation of inhibitory G i/o proteins accounts for the hallucinogenic properties of psychedelics.

title: The molecular and neurochemical basis of altered intrinsic neural timescales in major depressive disorder: a multimodal imaging-transcriptomic investigation of esketamine and sertraline treatment.
post: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is characterized by dysfunction in higher-order cortical regions involved in emotional and cognitive processes; however, its neurobiological basis remains unclear. Pharmacological treatments, including esketamine and sertraline, produce rapid antidepressant effects.

title: Gi Signaling Does Not Differentiate Hallucinogenic from Nonhallucinogenic 5-HT2A Receptor Agonists.
post: A recent publication by Xu et al. suggests that Gi activation following 5-HT2AR stimulation differentiates hallucinogenic from nonhallucinogenic agonists. Here, we reanalyze the author's source data to demonstrate that Gi activation is less predictive of hallucinogenic potential than canonical effectors of 5-HT2AR signaling.

title: Psychedelic modulation of excitation–inhibition balance and the Affective Core Self: A multilevel mechanistic framework
post: Serotonergic psychedelics reliably alter affective tone, emotional regulation, and self-experience. Prevailing theories emphasize acute changes in neural entropy, default mode network integrity, and large-scale functional connectivity but do not offer a clear mechanism that explains how 5-HT2A receptor pharmacology relates to lasting changes in affect and self-related processing.

title: Rapid antidepressant effects of psilocybin without increased SV2A binding: baseline binding predicts response
post: We report a pre-registered [11C]UCB-J PET sub-study of a recently published randomized trial in which a single psilocybin dose produced rapid and sustained antidepressant effects in major depressive disorder (MDD).
